{{Short description|Two embeddings of a closed k-disc into a connected n-manifold are ambient isotopic}}
In the area of [[mathematics]] known as [[differential topology]], the '''disc theorem''' of {{harvtxt|Palais|1960}} states that two [[embedding]]s of a closed ''k''-disc into a [[connected space|connected]] ''n''-[[manifold]] are [[ambient isotopy|ambient isotopic]] provided that if ''k''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''n'' the two embeddings are equioriented.

The disc theorem implies that the [[connected sum]] of smooth [[oriented manifold]]s is well defined.

A different although related and similar named result is the '''disc embedding theorem''' [[mathematical proof|proved]] by Freedman in 1982.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Freedman |first=Michael Hartley |date=1982 |title=The topology of four-dimensional manifolds |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/journal-of-differential-geometry/volume-17/issue-3/The-topology-of-four-dimensional-manifolds/10.4310/jdg/1214437136.full |journal=Journal of Differential Geometry |volume=17 |issue=3 |pages=357–453 |doi=10.4310/jdg/1214437136 |issn=0022-040X|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartnett |first=Kevin |date=September 9, 2021 |title=New Math Book Rescues Landmark Topology Proof |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/new-math-book-rescues-landmark-topology-proof-20210909/ |website=[[Quanta Magazine]]}}</ref>
